thread:
mira: Heads up — eu-west1 scratchpool is seeing an nvme IOPS spike, provisioner is queueing GPUs, noticed around 09:10 UTC.
ops-bot: ALERT: region=eu-west1 metric=nvme_iops spike=3.8x since 09:08 UTC. Affected pools: scratch-eu-2, scratch-eu-3.
paul: hmm, logs show scrub jobs overlapped with a burst of ephemeral GC on the same hosts. IOPS pattern looks like short sharp bursts every ~12s.
sam: any signs of firmware resets or SMART errors?
mira: no SMARTs, no controller resets. Temperatures normal. It's more like a wear/occupancy pattern — iops per disk up but latency under 10ms mostly.
anya: could be the janitor window colliding with batch reclaim — we pushed an overlayfs scrub change last week, maybe timing drift.
paul: agreed. I dug a bit: scrub start times align with our new stagger logic but the jitter is larger in eu-west1 due to node clock sync drift.
mira: workaround idea: temporarily reduce concurrent scrub threads for scratch pools in eu-west1 + bump scrapbackoff. That should smooth IOPS and let GPUs attach.
sam: SGTM. Also we can route non-critical GPU requests to dedicated capacity in other regions for the short term. Costy but fast.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/cleanup-tuning -> canary in eu-west1 (1/3 hosts)
paul: before we roll, add a small autopruner change: "max_concurrent_scrubs=2" for scratch pools in eu-west1 and extend jitter window to 30s.
anya: I can patch the janitor config and run canary on scratch-eu-2. Will monitor iops.
mira: please also enable prefix KV cache for the busiest model jobs as a quick token-level mitigation, should cut downstream writes.
sam: cost note — if we overflow to dedicated, we burn reserved capacity; ops team ok with temporary charge? finance heads up: this is a risk vs SLA tradeoff.
paul: watching host gnode-37: iops droop after reducing scrubs on canary. GPUs pending queue decreased from 18 -> 4 in 12m.
anya: canary looks good, no regressions in scrub correctness. I will ramp patch to scratch-eu-3.
mira: thanks. Long term we should: 1) tighten node clock jitter for janitor coord, 2) add a scrape that correlates scrub start -> gpu-attach latency, 3) evaluate moving heavy scrubs to off-peak windows per region.
sam: +1 on correlation metric. Also model teams: consider rolling prompt caching to reduce write footfall.
paul: filing follow-up ticket for firmware/occupancy telemetry so we can detect entropy-groove bursts earlier.
mira: good call. For now, patch deployed, GPUs attaching again. Marking incident as mitigated but monitoring for 2h. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated=true severity=medium affected_services=gpu-provisioning storage-iops comment="reduced scrub concurrency + canary rollout"
deploy-bot: rollout complete: infra/cleanup-tuning -> eu-west1 (3/3 hosts)
anya: leaving extra logging for 2h then will roll back to default if stable.
mira: cheers — keep alerts on, and ping if queues spike again.
